text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Four judges of the Constitutional court were sworn in by President Guntis Ulmanis.

- Two of parliament's opposition factions, the Socialist Party and the Movement for Latvia, have asked for a vote of no-confidence in state revenue minister Aija Pocha for allowing the seizure of a transit cargo of alchohol.
- During his visit to Moscow, Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans agreed to repay the debts of former national airline Latavio, opening the way for new state carrier Air Baltic to fly to Moscow.
- Parliament today starts consideration of the second and final reading of the 1997 budget, which may take two days.
- Two hospitals in Riga had their heating cut off for at least two hours as they have run up debts to the state heating company.

- Deputy Parliament speaker Andris Ameriks and the chairman of the European Affairs committee, Edvins Inkens, announced at a press conference after their return from the WEU General Assembly in Paris that NATO is in the process of discussing the conclussion of a special treaty with Russia but it was not clear whether the Baltic States will be admitted to NATO in the first stage of its expansion.
- The foreign ministry has so far received no official note from Scandinavian countries immigration services confirming their readiness to receive 108 Asian refugees from Latvia.

- State-owned oil terminal group Ventspils Nafta organised a seminar on the island of Madeira to talk about its privatisation and future with Russian and Western companies involved in the oil transport business.
- An international seminar of the North-Atlantic Assembly was held in Riga. It was attended by representatives of 12 nations, including six NATO members.
